For vendors

Your customer asked for an examination

A customer, insurer or investor asked us to examine the evidence behind a claim you make. Here's what happens, what you'll be asked for, and your rights.

What happens

  1. You're told which claim is being examined, and for what scope.
  2. The examiner asks for the evidence behind that claim, and sends written questions.
  3. You answer in writing.
  4. The examiner signs the findings, a second reviewer releases them, and the report goes to the party who asked for the check.

Your rights

  • You can answer every question in writing.
  • You can't edit a finding.
  • The report goes only to the party who asked for the check.
  • The examiner and the reviewer write down their ties to you before work starts.
  • We don't name a vendor beside a failure, and I won't publish a verdict on any named party.
Why it can help you

A checked claim is easier to rely on

A claim whose evidence has been examined by someone who doesn't work for you is one a careful buyer can rely on. The Casebook counts claims that held as well as cases where AI errors caused harm.

See the Casebook

Asked to take part in an examination?

Write to us with any question about the process, before or during the work.
